A very spectacular display of Aurora Borealis during the evening of the 26-27 a.m. It was extraordinarily brilliant for this section. From 9:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. the aurora occupied practically all quadrants of the sky, converging to a point near the zenith. Purple, red, green and pink colors were observed. Flickering or sort of a wave motion was noted during the display.
Aurora continued from midnight till 12:25 a.m., when obscured by clouds. Observed again from 3:15 a.m. to 3:55 a.m.
A brief display of the Aurora Borealis, without coloration, was seen in the late evening of the 30th.
An Aurora in the form of pulsating white streamers was observed in the north at 11:35 p.m. on the 30th and continued until 2:15 a.m. on the 31st.

Only one auroral display was observed. Beginning at 10:10 p.m. on the 30th and ending at 4:30 a.m. on the 31st brilliant green white searchlight streamers moved frequently to about 50o above the southern horizon.
Aurora Borealis observed from 11:20 p.m. till 2:45 a.m. of the 31st. No details recorded.
Aurora, 2000, thin veil about 45o high, northern sky, little movement.
There were five days with displays of the Aurora Borealis. None of these was particularly spectacular, having no colors other than green-white and streamers did not reach beyond the zenith.
The Aurora Borealis was seen briefly on the evening of the 17th and of the 18th.

Two auroras were observed during the month. The first one, which began at 9:35 p.m. on the 17th and continued until 3:50 a.m. on the 18th, was in the nature of a curtain with white, red, green and yellow streamers pulsating from it and had an altitude of 90 degrees.
Aurora - began as patches and veils in northeast about 1930, gradually spread over sky and then dwindled to a low arch in the southeast at 2200.

A display of Aurora Borealis was observed from 8:15 p.m. through midnight, first appearing as an auroral arch between az. 230o and 270o and at a height of about 15o to 20o. It was most extensive at 10:00 p.m., when streamers and sheets extended from the horizon in west and east quadrants, with green and blue colors in easterly quadrant. They merged in a yellowish spiral just west of the zenith.
The second one, [see entry for 9/17 for first one] which began at 10:10 p.m. and ended at 11:10 p.m. on the 18th, was white and much less vivid than the first. It reached an altitude of 40 degrees.
An auroral arch was again visible from 7:45 p.m. to 8:30 p.m., from about az. 140o to 210o. Streamers rose at times from this arch and extended to a height of approximately 40o.
Aurora - around 2300 - sheets and curtains high in the sky.
Aurora - streamers and curtains NE to NW starting about 10o high and mounting to zenith, evening, obscured by clouds at about 2020.
Aurora Borealis observed from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. A greenish glow was visible in the north, with an arch from 8:10 p.m. on.
An unspectacular aurora occurred during the night of the 1st.
About 1 a.m. of the 9th a brilliant display was noted. Rapidly moving bright green bands appeared in the north and northeast with tops of the streamers just short of the zenith.

The aurora on the 19th was merely a glow on the northern horizon during the evening. That on the 26th was an arch from northwest to northeast about 20o high at the center with many short streamers it began at 1800.
That [the aurora] on the 26th was an arch from northwest to northeast about 20o high at the center with many short streamers it began at 1800.
Aurora Borealis observed 9:20-10:15 p.m. through ground fog - no details given concerning extent.
Another display appeared just after dusk of the 31st. This consisted of a bright white light behind alto-cumulus clouds.
Several auroras were observed, none spectacular. These were low on the northern horizon and pale green white, with no streamers. [Note: dates from monthly summary]
The aurora on the 15th was in the form of a pale glow on the northern horizon.
Aurora Borealis observed 4:10 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. No details recorded of manifestations.

Only one occurrence of the northern lights was noted. It began at dusk on the 19th as an arc from NW to E, running through Polaris. At 9 p.m. colored search light rays with some red bands danced across the arc. The display ended shortly before midnight.
Only one aurora occurred, this during the night of the twelfth and it had little color.
A faint aurora after sunset on the 18th became flashing after midnight with brilliant colors, covering most of the sky and was still visible up till dawn.

Aurora Borealis observed 1950 to 2300. It was most brilliant between 2100 and 2200. The center of the display was somewhat east of north and was in the form of an auroral arch, with the base extending along the horizon about ninety degrees. The points of greatest brilliance were constantly changing in position on the arch, with streamers of varying lengths occasionally reaching the zenith. The predominating color was pinkish, but yellow and green colors were observed during the display.
Auroras were observed on the 8th, 15th, 19th, 26th, 27th and 28th. No descriptions were obtained of the faint displays on the 8th and 15th.
Aurora Borealis displays occurred on the 15th and the 27th of March.
The aurora of the 15th. reached to a hight of 70o above the north to west horizon. Mostly red in north and west with Fluctuating bands of white.
The aurora of the 19-20 was not spectacular being very low on the horizon (northern) and pale white in color.
A faint homogeneous arc was observed between 2310 and 2355 on the 19th. The greatest elevation was 18 degrees, and the horizontal extent from 330 to 30 degrees.
The display of the 26th lasted from 0001 to 0055, but probably began earlier than the observation indicates. A medium, greenish-white glow; altitude 30 degrees, azimuth 350 to 45 degrees.
The aurora of the 27-28 was also pale and very low on the horizon.
A medium white glowing arc was observed between 0203 and 0440 on the 27th. Altitude 20 degrees, azimuth 350 to 70 degrees.
The display of the 28th was observed between 0001 and 0440. Medium white; altitude 35 degrees, azimuth 340 to 50 degrees.
Aurora Borealis observed 0020 to 0120. No details given of phenomena.
Aurora was observed on the 14th and 15th.
Auroral displays on the 14th, 15th and 16th were unspectacular.

Auroras were observed on the 14th, 15th, 22nd, (extending into the morning of the 23rd), and the 31st. The display of the 14th was a faint homogeneous arc, elevation 20 degrees, azimuth 330 to 60 degrees. This was observed between 2245 and 2350 EST.
Aurora Borealis 2200 to 2345; no details given of manifestations.
A faint arc with streamers was reported between 2240 and 2355 on the 15th; elevation 28 degrees, azimuth 270 to 50 degrees.
The Aurora Borealis was observed on two days this month. The display of the 16th extended to 30o above the horizon. Plumes and wisps were seen; mostly white, with some orange.
Another arc with streamers on the 22nd and 23rd; elevation at maximum 80 degrees, azimuth 290 to 50 degrees. This was observed between the hours of 2245 and 0150.
Northern Lights were also observed on the 24th.

A display of the Aurora Borealis occurred on May 24th. There were parallel bands of light, mostly white, with occasionally faint red and green color. The display was visible from Northwest to Northeast and approached the zenith.
Aurora Borealis observed from 2200, continued at midnight. No details given of manifestations.

The display of rays on the 31st began at 2240 and continued into the morning of June 1st. Elevation 75 degrees, azimuth 340 to 60 degrees. In each case the color observed was whitish, but some observers reported a reddish glow with the display of the 22nd and 23rd.
Aurora borealis continued from May 31st until 0230. No details of phenomenon noted.

Auroras were observed on the 1st., 13th., 16th., and 17th. All were faint except the display of the 13th. which produced brilliant green and red rays converging at zenith. The display of the 1st., which was a continuation of that reported on May 31st., ended at 0100. The display of June 13th. began at 2115 and was obscured slowly by advancing cloudiness. Azimuth range was 280 to 020 degrees, elevation zenith.
A weak aurora was visible during the night of the 12th.
An Auroral display was observed on the 13th.

A vivid aurora occurred the following night [i.e., the 13th] with brilliant streamers reaching to well south of the zenith. Most color was green-white but there were some pinkish hues. Frequent very bright spots with fluctuating streamers moved back and forth rapidly. [Note: monthly summary also lists an aurora for 6/14. It is taken here as a continuation of the aurora of the evening of the 14th.]
Aurora borealis observed from 2300 to 2340. No details of phenomenon noted.
Aurora borealis observed from  0100 to 0130. No details of phenomenon noted.

The display of the 16th. and 17th. began at 2303 on the 16th. as a faint glow and continued as a rayed arc after 0045 on the 17th., ending at 0245. The greatest horizontal extent was 340 to 045 degrees, elevation 25 degrees.
[monthly summary only] Seven days with auroras were observed. [Note: dates in following for August are from monthly summary.]

A  spectacular auroral display occurred during the night of the 11th. The aurora began at 10 p.m. as a low band in the north. Distinct searchlight rays became cloud-like, fading and brightening, with red colored rotating arcs. Green and blue beams were not noted at 11 p.m. The display blotted out stars at times during a Perseid shower. The display grew weaker just before midnight and ended about 2:30 a.m.

Auroras were observed on the eleventh, seventeenth and twenty-second, carrying over in each case into the succeeding day. In each case whitish rays were observed. Elevation and azimuth readings were: 40 degrees, 315-060 degrees; 45 degrees, 350-70 degrees; and 40 degrees, 290-90 degrees respectively.
A white and red display of the Aurora Borealis was observed on August 12.
Aurora borealis observed from 0015 until 0030. No special characteristics noted.
There were unspectacular displays on the 13th and the 20th.
Four displays of Aurora Borealis were observed in September. They occurred on Sept. 3, 13, 14, and 23.
Elevation 35 deg., Azimuth 300-45 deg., faint red and white rayed arc.
Three Auroras were observed during the month. One on the 6th, was very bright with pulsating arc and a brillent red color.
Aurora Borealis observed from 2135 until 2245; no special characteristics.
Elevation 60 deg., Azimuth 320-45 deg., greenish-white rayed arc. (continued on 17th.)
Elevation 30 deg., Azimuth 345-45 deg., faint whitish rays. (continued on 18th.)
The Aurora Borealis was observed briefly on the 23rd.
Aurora Borealis observed from 0200 until 0400; visible low in northern horizon. Display generally weak and intermittent; brightest display observed from 0215 to 0220.
Elevation 25 deg., Azimuth 310-50 deg., bright, whitish rayed arc.
Elevation 20 deg., Azimuth 350-50 deg., faint whitish arc.
Several unspectacular auroras were visible during the month. On the 30th. there was a brief display of bright greenish streamers reaching about 45o above the horizon just before midnight.
Aurora Borealis (faint) observed from 2245 until about 2320; height of curtain base 9o.

Elevation 45 deg., Azimuth 300-50 deg., faint whitish rays. Auroras were quite frequent with 8 be observed. [Note: dates in following taken from monthly summary.] Auroras were observed on the 2nd., the 8th. through the 15th., and the 20th. through the 22nd. Of these the display of the 21st. was merely a continuation of that of the 20th.
Two displays of Aurora Borealis were observed on October 2 and 10.

Aurora Borealis observed from 2200 on the 2nd until 0120 on the 3rd. Bands of pulsating light at 22:30 extended from the northern sky Az. 135o to 225o at times nearly to the zenith, apparently drifting from east to west. But little color was noted, possibly because of the brilliance of the moonlight.
Elev. 15 deg., Azimuth 050-070 deg.; faint reddish & whitish rays.
An auroral display beginning just before midnight on the 8th and ending at dawn had bright streamers reaching to 30 degrees above the horizon.
Elev. 25 deg., Azimuth 340-050 deg.; faint whitish arc.
Another during night of the 9th had very bright streamers reaching to the zenith.
Aurora Borealis observed, brilliant, from 1945 to 1950, then dim to 2010 on the 9th; observed again as long arch NW through NNE from 2340 on the 9th until 0400 on the 10th.
Elev. 40 deg., Azimuth 335-080 deg.; reddish & whitish rays, medium bright to bright.
The Aurora Borealis was seen in two weak displays on the 10th and 11th.
Elev. 20 deg., Azimuth 010-090 deg.; faint white homogeneous arc.
Elev. 20 deg., Azimuth 010-080 deg.; faint whitish rayed arc.
Elev. 15 deg., Azimuth 360-040 deg.; faint whitish rayed arc.
Elev. 20 deg., Azimuth 345-045 deg.; faint whitish rayed arc.
Less brilliant display occurred on the 14th, 15th and 16th.
Elev. 15 deg., Azimuth 360-040 deg.; faint whitish homogeneous arc.
Elev. 30 deg., Azimuth 345-040 deg.; faint whitish rayed arc.
Elev. 05 deg., Azimuth 320-030 deg.; faint whitish homogeneous arc.
Elev. 15 deg., Azimuth 320-015 deg.; faint whitish band.
Two Auroral displays were observed on the 9th and 10th.
Aurora Borealis observed from 2015 to 2030; diffuse NW to NE, altitude 45o.

Auroras were observed on the 9th, 10th, and 16th. All were faint whitish rayed arcs. Angular measurements were: 9th., elevation 60 degrees, azimuth 300-040 degrees; 10th., elevation 30 degrees, azimuth 320-030 degrees; 16th., elevation 15 degrees, azimuth 350-050 degrees.
Faint auroras occurred on the 15th and 19th.
A display of Aurora Borealis was observed on November 19.
Aurora Borealis observed from 0400 to 0415; faint glow low on horizon to north, occasional longitudinal plumes.
Aurora borealis observed (faint) from 0400 to 0605. No special characteristics.
An Aurora was observed on the 15th.
Auroras were observed on the 15th., a faint arc of 15 degrees elevation and azimuth 340 to 40 degrees, which continued into the 16th;
the 27th., a faint greenish-white band with rays having an elevation of 15 degrees and azimuth 350 to 45 degrees;
and the 29th., a medium bright greenish-white homogeneous band of elevation 15 degrees, and azimuth 350 to 40 degrees.
Auroras were observed on the first, thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth. The display of the first was a continuation of that reported on February twenty-ninth.
That of the thirteenth which was continued on the fourteenth was a faint homogeneous arc, the greatest elevation being 30 degrees, and azimuth 340 to 030 degrees.
One Aurora was observed on the 14th.
An aurora was observed on the 15th from 0210 to 0435. It was in the form of steady streamers of a greenish white color, with an occasional reddish tinge.
Aurora borealis observed 0000-0400; faint through W, NW, to NE.
A rayed arc, azimuth 335 to 045 degrees and reaching the zenith, was observed on the fifteenth.
An aurora was observed from 11:50 p.m. on the 21st to 1:45 a.m. on the 22nd. It was in the form of pulsating faint white streamers extending from 45 to 55 degrees above the horizon.
Only one auroral display was observed. Flashing streamers and brilliant colors were observed most of the night of the 21st.

Auroras were observed on the 2nd. and 15th., that of the 2nd. continuing into the 3rd., and the display of the 15th. continuing on the 16th. The first of these was a faint whitish rayed arc of elevation 20 degrees nd azimuth 330 to 030 degrees.
Aurora began 11:15 p.m. on the 15th, ended 3:10 a.m. on the 16th. It was in the nature of greenish white streamers to an elevation of 40 degrees from northwest through northeast.
An Aurora was observed on the 15th.

A brilliant auroral display was observed through the night of the 15th. No colors were seen but bright streamers rose from practically the entire azimuth and converged about 10 degrees south of the zenith.
Aurora observed 2305 until 0325 a.m. of 16th. (No special characteristics)

That of the 15th. and 16th. began as a faint whitish homogeneous band of elevation 15 degrees and azimuth 360 to 045 degrees, and developed brilliant white rays reaching the zenith and widening to 300 to 090 degrees azimuth.
An aurora was observed on the 29th. A faint whitish glow of elevation 10 degrees and azimuth 330 to 020 degrees was observed between 0100 and 0210.
On the 7th and 8th the Aurora Borealis was visible

Aurora Borealis began 11:30 p.m. on the 7th and ended 4:05 a.m. on the 8th. It extended from northwest to northeast and reached an elevation of 35 degrees, with pulsating shafts reaching to the zenith, occasionally tinted red and green.
An Aurora was observed on the 7th.
Weak auroras were observed on the 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11th.

An interesting auroral display was observed on the 7th. and 8th., consisting of parallel arcs which developed rays and finally a corona. Starting at azimuth 300 to 040 degrees, this display finally covered all the northern half of the sky, passing beyond the zenith to elevation 150 degrees from north. Color whitish and becoming bright in intensity by 0330 on the 8th.

Aurora borealis observed from 0040 to 0355. From 0040 to 0130 it was of moderate brilliance and in the form of an arc; from 0130 to 0210 it displayed shimmering waves almost to the zenith with stationary lights just over the zenith to the south; from 0210 to 0300 the brilliance of the aurora diminished somewhat but it was still shimmering at low angles to the north; From 0300 to 0330 the display was most brilliant with rays and curtains in a quasi-trapezoidal shape, extending in its most brilli
A whitish rayed arc of azimuth 300 to 050 degrees and elevation 32 degrees was observed on the 8th., and continued into the morning of the 9th.
Aurora Borealis began 1:00 a.m. and ended 3:55 a.m. on the 10th. Faint glow occasionally pulsating with shafts reaching to 40 degrees.

Aurora borealis observed from 0050 to 0335. The aurora was faint from 0050 to 0130 and in the form of an arc above the northern horizon; from 0130 to 0145 shimmering was noted about half way to the zenith; from 0145 to 0200 it was of moderate brilliance in the form of rays shimmering to about a 60o elevation; from 0200 to 0335 there was an arc to the north with faint shimmering above; the aurora faded as daylight approached.
A faint whitish homogeneous arc of azimuth 350 to 040 degrees and elevation 12 degrees was observed on the 10th.
A faint whitish glow of azimuth 010 to 045 degrees and elevation 15 degrees was observed on the 11th.
A greenish-white homogeneous arc of medium brightness, azimuth 350 to 050 degrees and elevation 12 degrees was observed on the 29th and continued into the morning of the 30th.
Aurora Borealis began 11:15 p.m. on the 31st, continued past midnight. Faint glow northwest to northeast.
A faint whitish glow of azimuth 350 to 030 degrees and elevation 25 degrees was observed on the 31st.
[monthly summary only] There were several unspectacular auroral displays during the month.
Aurora borealis (faint) observed from 0015 to 0145. No special characteristics noted.

Auroras were observed on the 1st, (continued on the 2nd), and 25th. That of the 1st was a faint whitish glow; elevation 15 degrees, azimuth 010 to 040 degrees, extending on th morning of the 2nd from 330 to 040 degrees.
The display of the 25th began as a medium, greenish-white rayed arc at 1940, and faded to a faint whitish glow by 2010. Elevation 20 degrees, azimuth 350 to 040 degrees.
The Aurora Borealis was observed on the 1st, 4th, 10th, 18th and 19th.
An Aurora Borealis was observed from 1:05 A to 2:15 A on the 2nd. It consisted of a faint glow with occasional pulsating streamers.
Aurora borealis observed from 0055 to 0115; of low brilliance, extending in a NNE-NNW arc and subtending an angle of approximately 20o.
Auroras were observed on the second, medium bright, whitish rays, elevation 85 degrees, azimuth 290 to 080 degrees;

Aurora Borealis was observed briefly late on the 4th and early on the 5th. The display was colored with yellows and greens; however since the aurora was observed only briefly and through broken clouds no other description could be obtained. [Note: monthly summary gives dates as October 17, 18. There is no obvious explanation for this discrepancy.]
Auroral displays were observed on 2 days. [Note: date from monthly summary]

the fourth, (continued on the fifth), two faint, whitish arcs, the morning display of elevation 30 degrees, azimuth 330 to 025 degrees, and the evening display of elevation 25 degrees, azimuth 330 to 020 degrees;
the tenth, a faint whitish arc of elevation 40 degrees, azimuth 325 to 030 degrees;
the fourteenth, a faint whitish arc with rays, elevation 75 degrees, azimuth 320 to 025 degrees;
Aurora borealis observed from 1915 to 1950; bar shaped, reddish glow, very faint, in NW direction; elevation angle approximately 75o.

An Aurora Borealis was observed from 11:15 P on the 18th to 4:45 A on the 19th. It extended from the northwest through the north with an elevation of 40 degrees. It consisted of white patches with pulsating yellow-pink streamers.
The display on the night of the 18th was marked by brilliant white streamers which met to the south of the zenith.

Aurora borealis observed from 1815 to 1835 (faint); again from 2015 to 2210; observed as a faint green yellow ray arc over 1/4 horizon from NNW to NNE, beginning at 2245 and continuing until 0300 on the 19th.

the eighteenth, (continued on the nineteenth and probably continuous but sometimes impossible to observe because of faintness and the interference of surrounding lights), elevation 15 to 40 degrees, azimuth variable between 320 and 040 degrees, a faint to occasionally medium bright arc with occasional rays;
Aurora borealis observed again as a faint green yellow band 90o overhead beginning at 0340 and ending at 0355.
the twenty-second, a faint whitish glow, elevation 10 degrees, azimuth 010 to 040 degrees.
an aurora was observed on the 1st.

Aurora Borealis displays. B 2200 - E 0410 of 2nd. Also on 2nd, B 2115 - E 2130. On 1st in the form of a faint greenish arch. At 2345, moving curtains or vertical streamers, one fold brilliant, and moving from north to north north-west, then fading. On the 2nd in the fomr of an arc of moderate brilliance and faint yellow-green in color.
Aurora began 6.20 p.m. - Faint arc, elevation 20 degrees. Azimuth 330 to 20 Degrees.
Borealis was observed from 2:10 A to 4:15 A on the 2nd. It was in nature of a faint glow in the north with an arc visible.
Aurora of day before ended at 1.00 a.m. Aurora again observed DNP, faint rayed arc 35o.
An aurora was observed on the twenty-third, (continued on the twenty-fourth), a faint, whitish arc, elevation 20 degrees, azimuth 340-015 degrees.

An aurora was observed on the 25th.
